title: Supplemental jurisdiction in diversity cases
summary: When original jurisdiction rests solely on diversity, § 1367(b) restricts certain additional claims by plaintiffs and proposed plaintiffs. The role of each party and the method of joinder matter.
notes: Do not treat every joined plaintiff or every third-party claim identically. Nor does satisfaction of one plaintiff’s amount eliminate all other jurisdictional defects.

sections.Meaning: When original jurisdiction rests solely on diversity, § 1367(b) restricts certain additional claims by plaintiffs and proposed plaintiffs. The role of each party and the method of joinder matter.
sections.How to work through the question: Apply § 1367(a) first. Then identify the specific claim and the listed joinder rule in subsection (b), and ask whether exercising jurisdiction would conflict with § 1332’s requirements. Exxon addresses related claims lacking the required amount while preserving the distinction from missing complete diversity.
